about: This site against Wikipedia, both ways. wikipedia_to_us: for each Wikipedia claim, the timeline row (by permanent id) that says the same, the data file that holds it, or that it is missing here. us_to_wikipedia: for each of our key facts, whether each language has the subject, whether it has our time, the revision in which it first appeared and whom it cites. Every relation is our analysis of two bodies of evidence; a pattern match on wikitext finds the subject, not agreement.
attribution: Wikipedia's text is by Wikipedia's contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/). Each statement here is our own English paraphrase; the anchor is a few words of the article, quoted to find the sentence; the exact revision is linked.

checks.about: What this team found when it went to the primary source for a Wikipedia statement. Wikipedia is a lead for us, never the source.

not_established.why: The count of ten is not established: the press we read says only that several TAP flights to Funchal were affected, from the airport operator's site; TAP's own statement is about rebooking (decision tap-adjusts).
As stated, not established: the order we could trace is national (court presidents may close courts fully or partly; decision csm-courts), not specific to Madeira. The 34 trials were not checked.
No such notice was found on the environment agency's own site by incident.researcher@ (01:45 to 01:50 UTC on 11 November). The figure rests on the radio report Wikipedia cites.
The Hurricane Center's own archived outlooks label the low AL94 on 6 November (11:37 UTC), not 7; and no source read says it became Charles (data/weather/analysis.md, section 8b, a hypothesis).

wikipedia_to_us.note: The six-hour maximum, 249.5 mm, is our row s-1111T0727 (IPMA's station Areeiro, read by us); the 24- and 12-hour totals are not on this site. Cited to the regional daily, not to IPMA's own data.
